Declared category levels from the public vocabulary

Source: R/concept_levels.R
omop_concept_levels.Rd

Expands a concept set on every connected server's vocabulary tables and returns the union as declared category keys for omop_category_spec(levels = ). The expansion reads only vocabulary reference tables (concept, concept_ancestor, concept_relationship), never patient rows.

Usage

omop_concept_levels(
  concept_set,
  symbol = "omop",
  conns = NULL,
  datasources = NULL
)

Arguments

concept_set

An omop_concept_set(); descendants, mapped and exclude expand as in an event.

symbol

Character; the OMOP session symbol.

conns

Deprecated alias of datasources, kept for backward compatibility (a one-time message names the new argument).

datasources

DataSHIELD connections (a named list of DSConnection objects). NULL (the default) uses the OMOP session's connections, or DSI::datashield.connections_find() when no session exists. See dsomop_conventions.

Value

Character vector of "concept:<id>" keys in concept ID order.

Details

Declared levels are public. A concept column presented with them is built from the declaration at every site, so nothing about which concepts occur at a site is released and no factor-level limit applies to them, however many levels the list holds. Observed values outside the list are still discovered under DataSHIELD's factor-level rule (nfilter.levels.max and nfilter.levels.density). Counts and models keep their usual disclosure controls.

The union covers sites whose vocabulary versions differ. The keys are stored in the recipe, so it records exactly which levels it declares.

See also

omop_category_spec, omop_concept_set

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
causes <- omop_concept_levels(omop_concept_set(4306655, descendants = TRUE))
cause <- omop_category(
  omop_variable(event = omop_event("death", name = "cause_of_death"),
                reducer = omop_reduce("first_value", value = "cause_concept_id")),
  omop_category_spec(levels = causes))
} # }
